Here it is considered view of the Tribunal that there is highly possibility/chances that the petitioners has got the abovementioned alleged medical bills/receipts reimbursed from other source like medical insurance or any other source, otherwise, what stopped the petitioner to produced/filed the original medical bills/receipts.
Further it is equally worthy to note here that it is well settled law that photocopy of document is not considered legally admissible in the absence of original of it.
In other words, photocopy is not sufficient to prove the alleged bills/receipts.
In these circumstances and in view of the material on record, the petitioner/injured is not entitled to towards 'medicines and medical treatment'.
12. CONVEYANCE & SPECIAL DIET:
Although the petitioner has not claimed conveyance and special diet but in the present case, as per the medical treatment record, petitioner/ injured is suffering from Right MACP No. 1536/16 Ram Kishan Vs. In these circumstances, the petitioner/injured must have visited the hospital/doctors for his treatment and would also have required special diet for certain period to recover from the injuries sustained in the accident.
However no evidence, documentary or otherwise, in this regard has been brought on record on behalf of the petitioner.
Further, it is pertinent to note that from the material on record, it is evident that the petitioner/injured is about 55 years old at the time of accident and has suffered permanent disability due Ram Krishan Pal Singh vs Kumud Chandra Joshi on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113676840/
10 to the injuries sustained in the accident in this case.
It is also settled law
that compensation to be awarded by the MACT must be just compensation and can also be more than the amount claimed.
The proposition draws support from the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of Ramla and others vs National Insurance Company Limited and other 1 and Kajal vs Jagdish Chand & Ors.2
Notwithstanding this, in the instant case, the perusal of the record reveals that petitioner / injured is suffering from Right Ankle and Subtalar Arthedesis with Permanent physical Disability of 58%
(Fifty Eight Percent) in relation to Right Lower Limb and has remained hospitalized for more than four months due to the said injuries sustained by him in the accident.
In these circumstances, the petitioner/ injured must have required the services of attendant for about nine months.
In the case titled as Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. vs Lalita3, it has been held by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that a victim cannot be deprived of compensation towards gratuitous services rendered by some of the family members.
It is well settled law that a photostat copy of a document is not admissible as evidence in the absence of original.
In light of above, in the absence of any documentary proof, the case will be decided on the basis of applicable minimum wages.
Hence, the minimum wages for unskilled person applicable in the State of Delhi when the accident took place (15.04.2011) shall be considered.
In the instant case, petitioner/injured has suffered grievous injuries in right lower limb and has remained hospitalized for more than four months .
In the present case as per medical record, petitioner/injuredRam Kishan has remained hospitalized for more than 4 months and as per the Disability Certificate issued by DDU Hospital, New Delhi , the petitioner / injured - Ram Kishan is suffering from Right Ankle and Subtalar Arthedesis with Permanent physical Disability of 58% (Fifty Eight Percent) in relation to Right Lower Limb.
The principles for determining functional disability resulting from permanent physical impairment have been laid MACP No. 1536/16 Ram Kishan Vs. Kumud Chandra and Ors. 25 down in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar4.
It is noteworthy that extent of physical impairment cannot automatically be taken to be the loss of earning capacity.
The nature of avocation in which the petitioner was involved has to be considered.
Needless to say, he would be hindered from driving due to disability in his left leg.
Thus, the functional disability of the petitioner is taken to be at 30%.
, the petitioner is also entitled to future prospects.
As per the settled law, for assessing the pain & sufferings, the following factors have to be taken into account :
(a) Nature of injury (b) Parts of body where injuries occurred (c) Surgeries, if any (d) Confinement in hospital (e) Duration of the treatment.
In the instant case, in view of the material/evidence on record, there is no element of doubt that the petitioner/injured has suffered grievous injuries on the right leg and operated thrice and has remained hospitalized for more than 4 months due to the said injuries sustained by him.
Petitioner /
injured has further suf fered permanent physical disability of 58% in relation to Right Lower Limb.
In these circumstances and in view of the law laid down in the case titled as Rekha Jain vs National Insurance Co. Ltd.7, the petitioner/injured is entitled to compensation on ac count of pain &
suffering due to the accident.
The petitioner/injured was about 55 years of age at the time of accident and has suffered suffered permanent physical disability of 58% in relation to Right Lower Limb and was hospitalized for more than 4 months due to the said injuries sustained in the accident.
He had to suffer from restricted function of his lower limb.
Needless to say that restricted movement is also likely to affect his overall health.
